Chapter 10: Matthew—From Outcast to Storyteller
Imagine starting life on the outside, always feeling like you just don’t belong. That was Matthew’s world. As a tax collector, folks saw him as a traitor—working for the very people who ruled over his own. He knew what it was like to be judged and left out.
So, when the invitation came to follow, it must’ve felt almost unreal. A chance to start fresh, to finally be included—can you picture how that must have felt?
Matthew’s transformation didn’t happen overnight. He carried plenty of baggage—his past mistakes, the side glances from others, all the doubts. Learning a new way of living wasn’t easy. But slowly, he found where he fit. He became the one who noticed things others missed. Careful, patient, always listening. And eventually, he started to write it all down.
What stands out in Matthew’s story is his empathy for people on the edges. He goes out of his way to show moments where boundaries are crossed, where those left out are welcomed in, where mercy wins over judgment.
He pays attention to the little things—a gentle touch, a kind word, a simple meal shared with someone nobody else would notice. Those moments matter, and Matthew made sure we’d see them.
His journey is a powerful reminder: nobody is too far gone for a fresh start. Your past? It doesn’t have to write your future. Most folks, when they’re labeled or pushed aside, just grow bitter. But Matthew took another route. He used what he’d been through to tell a story filled with hope, inclusion, and real change.
So, if you’ve ever felt like you don’t fit in, Matthew’s life quietly encourages you. There’s always room at the table. There’s always a new beginning waiting for you.
